title: Multi-language SDK local-first playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, pragmatic playbook to onboard engineers to Redwood SDKs in a local-first, multi-language workflow. Focus: first 30–90 minutes to a running demo + deterministic failure modes for quicker debugging. This is intentionally opinionated — aim is to reduce friction during early experiments and to create reproducible dev loops for SDK maintainers and adopters.

Audience:
- Engs and ML Engs trying SDKs (JS/Python/Go) for the first time
- Solutions/SEs running hands-on demos with customers
- DX engineers who maintain starter repos and template CI

Success metrics (first milestone):
- Developer can run a local example that calls the Redwood hosted API or local simulator in under 30 min
- Clear reproducible steps to exercise auth, streaming, and error handling
- A triage checklist that surfaces 90% of onboarding failures in under 10 minutes

High-level flow (30m -> 90m):
1) 0–10m: Install minimal toolchain & clone language template (JS/Py/Go)
2) 10–25m: Configure credentials + run dev proxy (if using local simulator)
3) 25–45m: Run example, hit a streaming response, and inspect logs/trace id
4) 45–90m: Introduce one change (prompt tweak, param change, model variant) and observe telemetry (latency, token counts)

Prereqs (local machine):
- Node 18+ for JS templates, Python 3.10+, Go 1.20+ (where relevant)
- Docker (optional) to run the local simulator/proxy
- REDWOOD_API_KEY (or REDWOOD_LOCAL=true for simulator mode)
- git, curl

Templates to use (current canonical):
- redwood-js-starter (typescript, streaming example)
- redwood-py-stub (sync/async examples + eval harness)
- redwood-go-client (simple request/response)

Quickstart (JS example — 15–25 minutes)
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-js-starter.git
2) cd redwood-js-starter && yarn install
3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_XXXX (or run with local simulator env)
4) yarn dev (starts local example server + hot reload)
5) Open http://localhost:3000/demo -> click "Generate" -> observe stream + trace id in console

Note: for 'local-first' run, start the lightweight simulator: docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/redwood-inference/dev-sim:latest and set REDWOOD_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080

Auth & Secrets patterns (opinionated):
- For quickstarts use a transient demo key with narrow scopes (created by DX)
- Recommend local env var named REDWOOD_API_KEY for parity across languages
- For longer-term examples show how to wire up .env.local or credential helpers (macOS keychain, pass)

Core walkthrough checks (what to verify after "Generate"):
- Response stream starts within expected latency (30–300ms for hosted sample)
- Trace id appears in console and in the Redwood Console UI
- Token usage reported in the example logs (tokens_consumed)
- Correct handling of end-of-stream and partial messages (no uncaught exceptions)

Deterministic failure modes and triage notes (fast checklist)
1) 401 / auth errors -> verify REDWOOD_API_KEY and token scopes; try curl -i $REDWOOD_BASE_URL/v1/ping with header Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY
2) 502 / connection refused -> is simulator running? docker ps; check REDWOOD_BASE_URL and proxy port
3) Empty/partial stream -> check network MTU/proxy TLS termination; reproduce with small sample prompt to isolate tokenization edge cases
4) High latency -> set DEBUG_HTTP=1 and inspect request timing; check if request routed to fallback model variant in Console
5) Unexpected model outputs (format drift) -> use a deterministic prompt and capture model_id + generation seed; file a regression eval against the prompt set

Cheat sheet commands (cross-language)
- Verify auth: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" $REDWOOD_BASE_URL/v1/ping
- Start simulator: docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/redwood-inference/dev-sim:latest
- Toggle verbose logs: export DEBUG=redwood:* or export REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1

Example snippet (pseudo) to show streaming handling in any SDK:
- Open connection -> send request with "stream": true -> for each chunk: write to UI buffer + flush -> on EOF: close connection and report tokens

Telemetry & observability (what to surface to the user)
- Show trace id and clickable Console link in the sample app
- Surface per-request token estimates + actual tokens after response
- Surface model variant selection and fallback reason if any

Developer experience rules-of-thumb (opinionated):
- Keep the first-run demo single-purpose: one button for streaming generation, one for embeddings, one for rerank. No feature overload.
- Defaults should favor lower cost and faster latency (small model, short max_tokens) to encourage iteration.
- Examples should be resilient: autop-retry on transient 5xx, clear error messaging for auth/policy issues.
- Include a reproducible failing example (e.g., malformed function call) so users can exercise error handling.

Testing & CI suggestions for SDK maintainers
- Add a smoke test that runs examples against the simulator in CI (10–20s each)
- Add a test that verifies the SDK surface for streaming edge cases (mid-stream cancel, partial payloads)
- Add a lightweight contract test comparing tokens_estimated vs tokens_actual over a small set of prompts

Known gaps & TODOs (near-term next steps)
- [ ] Create transient demo keys automation (DX infra) to avoid manual key provisioning
- [ ] Standardize REDWOOD_BASE_URL and simulator image tag across templates
- [ ] Add one-click run in Codespaces / Gitpod to remove local setup friction
- [ ] Document model-variant naming conventions (hosted vs fallback) in README snippets

Open questions (for triage meeting):
- Do we prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY or language-specific env var (REDWOOD_JS_KEY etc.) for clarity vs consistency?
- Should the default quickstart use simulator or hosted sample key? Tradeoff: reproducibility vs measuring real latency/cost.

Appendix: common failure log excerpts and suggested fixes
- "Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8080" -> means simulator not running; start docker simulator or update REDWOOD_BASE_URL
- "401 Unauthorized - missing scope" -> regenerate demo key with `generate:examples` scope (DX CLI)
- "stream aborted by server" -> check server logs for backpressure/circuit-breaker events; reduce concurrency in example app

Next steps owner/action items:
- Maya: wire up Codespace template + update README (ETA 2 weeks)
- Evan: add simulator health endpoint and small payload benchmarks (ETA 3 weeks)
- Priya: add CI smoke job and integrate transient key rotation (ETA 4 weeks)

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep wording concise in readmes; developers skim — lead with "run these 3 commands".
- Timebox the onboarding script to sub-30s install where possible (use CDN deps in web demo).
- Collect first-run UX metrics: how many devs needed >15min to get example running?

End of draft.

History: started as notes from DX pairing session 2025-09-10; iterated after workshop with SEs 2025-11; last edited while building Codespaces template 2026-02-18.
